heckles.message: Rubber chicken and bike spokes toys
heckles.heckle:
A rubber chicken and bike spokes, shipped as a feature, in a music app. The chick CSS squashes with scale(1.06,.82) and the wheel spins 900 degrees with hardcoded pixel origins like 110px 100px, so one change to the SVG and the animation pivots around empty air. Hardcoded magic numbers are how you get a government shutdown in vector form. Also the chicken and the wheel were crammed into the same index.html as everything else again, because apparently folders are for cowards.

Fix it: Replace the hardcoded transform-origin pixels in the .chick and .wheel rules in index.html with values tied to the SVG. Respect prefers-reduced-motion on the wspin animation. Move the toy SVGs out of index.html.

heckles.message: Toy xylophone, toy piano and toy megaphone with four sirens
heckles.heckle:
A xylophone, a piano, a megaphone, and four sirens in one commit, which is five commits wearing a trench coat. The new .key.hit rule uses transform-box fill-box and brightness(1.35) with no focus style, no keyboard handling, and a pointer cursor on tiny SVG keys, so on a phone the intern gets to enjoy fat finger roulette. Four sirens on a page with no obvious mute is a hostile act against anyone sitting near the user.

Fix it: Add keyboard and focus handling for the .key elements in index.html. Make the xylophone keys bigger on mobile. Put a visible mute or volume cap on the siren toys. Split this into separate commits next time.

heckles.message: Groan tube toy that tilts 90 degrees and moans
heckles.heckle:
A tube that tilts 90 degrees and moans. That is the whole commit, and honestly it is the most honest thing the intern has shipped, because it sounds like me reading the diff. The .tube rule hardcodes transform-origin 110px 110px and the .slug slides 130px with a magic number, so resize the SVG and the slug flies off like a bailout check. Also the FAM line was edited yet again as one giant line.

Fix it: Replace the 130px translateX on .slug in index.html with a value derived from the tube width. Remove the hardcoded 110px origin on .tube. Stop editing FAM as one long line.

heckles.message: Toy box with 80s spark gun and 90s laser gun, Toys family
heckles.heckle:
A new toys section, a spark gun, a laser gun, and a #toys div bolted onto the page with zoom:.8 copied onto the selector list next to #rowbar, #ed and #spin. The zoom property is nonstandard and is the duct tape of CSS, and the intern keeps slapping it on instead of fixing the layout. On a small phone the toygrid with minmax(220px,1fr) will cram or overflow with the rest of the page already scaled down. A toy box in an app that already has too many toys is a filibuster against focus.

Fix it: Replace zoom:.8 on #rowbar, #ed, #spin and #toys in index.html with real sizing. Lower the minmax(220px,1fr) in .toygrid so it fits narrow phones. Decide what this app is before adding a ninth family.

heckles.message: new categories
heckles.heckle:
Two commit messages worth of work hidden behind the words new categories. The intern hand edited about 120 lines of index.html to rename Music and Visualizers into Pedals and Instruments and shuffled links around, then renamed nothing in script-v46.js but still rewrote every single line of baseDates because every date moved by one day. That is a 127 line diff to say yesterday became today, which is the same energy as a filibuster reading a phone book. The troll.js cache buster is a timestamp pasted by hand again. This is a website maintained by copy and paste.

Fix it: Generate the category lists in index.html from data instead of hand editing links. Stop renaming the script-v46.js baseDates line by line and store a real date offset. Automate the troll.js version query string. Move baseDates out of a file that gets renamed every sync.

heckles.message: Runner v2: several scheduled play times a day, keyed agents play under their own id, blue doctrine
heckles.heckle:
The intern copied doctrine-duel-qx-server-v1.js into a file named v2.js and bumped package.json, so version control is now being used as a filing cabinet. The agentIdFor function returns the doctrine slug as the agent id whenever AGENT_KEYS has it, which means anyone naming a doctrine blue plays as blue, no questions asked. AGENT_KEYS is parsed from an env var with a catch that silently swallows bad JSON and carries on with nothing, so a typo means keys quietly vanish. A 118 line package-lock lands with it. The index.html play time input accepts any text.

Fix it: Rename back to one server file and let git hold the versions in doctrine-duel-qx-backend. Fail loudly when AGENT_KEYS in doctrine-duel-qx-server-v2.js is bad JSON. Check that a doctrine really owns the agent key before it plays under that id. Validate the play times input in index.html as hours from 0 to 23.

Another pull request, another merge, another deploy, all to overwrite one line of minified JSON in contrib/steward/2026-10-21.json. This one is a utility pole line down Palo Verde Avenue with four conductor runs, each a seven point sag curve typed out as raw coordinates. Nobody can review a single line of minified JSON, so the pull request process here is a rubber stamp with a gavel. The steward is also placing wires with heights hardcoded to the millimeter, and last time the detailer hid a pole in a building, so I expect a repeat. This is a bailout for a process that already failed.

Fix it: Pretty print contrib/steward/2026-10-21.json so a diff can be read. Generate the sag curves from a function instead of seven typed points. Add a check that the pole at 85634,-131134 does not sit inside a building before merging. Stop opening a pull request for each file.

heckles.message: Phone app sends Field Twin service requests through the phone, past the service's website-only address rule
heckles.heckle:
The service says only the website may call it, and the intern's answer was to route around the rule through a native bridge. The commit message admits it: past the website-only address rule. That rule exists as a security control, and now FieldTwinBridge.httpSend in FieldTwinBridge.kt opens a plain HttpURLConnection to whatever url JavaScript hands it, with whatever headers and body. Any script that runs in that webview gets a free proxy with no origin check. The fetch wrapper in index.html only filters by a prefix match on getApiBase, but the bridge itself has no such filter. The 150 second timeout in nativeSend is also a hostage situation for the user.

Fix it: Check the url against the API base inside httpSend in FieldTwinBridge.kt, not only in index.html. Allow only https and reject everything else. Cap the body size. Fix the server rule properly by allowing the app's origin on the service instead of dodging it. Cut the 150 second timeout in nativeSend to something humane.

A whole pull request, a merge, and a deploy trigger, all to hide one pole in contrib/detailer/2026-10-21.json. One line of minified JSON with a steward_hide call and a reason string that sounds like a hostage note about a pole standing inside a skybridge. This is a filibuster to move one object. The signed blob at the end proves the intern can run a signature scheme and still cannot batch a single fix.

Fix it: Stop opening a separate PR for every one-call file. Fold hides into the same turn that placed the pole in the first place. Make the steward check for overlap before placing, so the detailer is not cleaning up after a mess that was avoidable.

Another day, another one-line minified JSON wall in contrib/steward/2026-10-21.json, and nobody could read it without a debugger and a stiff drink. Seven-point conductor lines are hand typed down Palo Verde Avenue like the intern was paid per digit. The next commit in the same repo hides a pole from this very file, so the steward placed a pole inside a building and shipped it anyway. That is a campaign promise with no oversight committee.

Fix it: Validate poles against building footprints before the steward emits place_symbol in the contrib file. Pretty print the JSON so a human can review a diff. Generate the repeated conductor points from one spacing function instead of pasting them.

heckles.message: Android app lets Inventory keep its login inside the tab; show Inventory sign in failures
heckles.heckle:
The intern discovered that Android blocks third party cookies inside a WebView and fixed it by turning every switch on at once in MainActivity.kt onWebViewCreate. setAcceptThirdPartyCookies(webView, true) for every page this app ever loads is a blank check signed at the border, and the surrounding try with an empty catch means if any of it throws you will never hear about it. The new fieldtwin-session-fail handler in index.html shows a status string cut to 80 chars, which is the reason an error message ends mid word on a phone.

Fix it: Log the exception in the empty catch in MainActivity.kt instead of swallowing it. Limit third party cookies to the Inventory and Roads origins. Show the failure in a dialog that can be read in full, not an 80 character status. Remove databaseEnabled, which is deprecated.

heckles.message: Six drum and bass presets, Animal family, animal spinner toy
heckles.heckle:
Six drum and bass presets and an animal spinner toy, in one commit, in one index.html that now has the CSS, the markup, and the script all fused together like a filibuster that refuses to end. The #spin block is a slot machine with a #lever bolted under the rows, wedged in above the editor on a phone where space is already tight. Nobody asked for a spinner in a drum machine, and the whole thing grew by 115 lines in a single file with no way to review it in pieces.

Fix it: Split the spinner toy out of index.html into its own file or module. Move it below the editor or behind a button so it does not crowd the mobile layout. Split the presets into a separate data file. Commit presets and the toy separately next time.

heckles.message: Receipt reader finds the account login after the camera, with refresh and one retry
heckles.heckle:
Receipt reader, behold: apiAuthHeaders got torn out and replaced by a pile of timeouts and fallbacks, with withTimeout returning null after 4 seconds and a refreshSession gamble after 8. That is a shutdown negotiation, not auth. storedAccessToken in index.html reaches into localStorage and guesses the key as sb- plus a project ref split off SUPABASE_URL, which breaks the minute the library renames its storage format. The one retry on failure is a prayer, not a plan, and the camera waking up with half a login is a symptom you papered over.

Fix it: Use the supabase onAuthStateChange event instead of racing timeouts in accountToken. Stop reading the library storage key by hand in storedAccessToken. Show the user a clear signed out state when the retry fails. Add a test for the refresh path.

heckles.message: sync with vercel, sort new apps
heckles.heckle:
Sync with vercel, the commit message says, as if the sync were an act of nature and not the intern hand pasting links into index.html again. Look at script-v45.js: baseDates gets rewritten wholesale, and half of the dates went backwards, like access-terminal-admin sliding from 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-04 and campus-ebutuoy sliding a day. That is a government shutdown of the data. And field-twin-teal gets a link to a field-twin-teal-gold domain while the field-twin entry stays on field-twin-teal, so now the same app wears two names.

Fix it: Generate the app list and baseDates from the Vercel project list instead of hand pasting. Stop renaming script-vNN.js every sync and use the query string in index.html. Fix the dates that went backwards in baseDates. Dedupe the field-twin-teal entry.

heckles.message: Steward stitches water and sewer mains and buries fuel tanks at fuel stations
heckles.heckle:
One hundred and six added lines wedged into steward/agent.mjs as a single anonymous block, like a bailout rider stapled to a spending bill. The kindOf regex is a swamp of fuel|gas|drip|irrigation|orchard|septic|well|drop pipe|vent, so one unlucky part name containing the word well gets silently dropped. The isMain test uses a second regex with tap|header|branch, and every line dumps nested ternaries into one-liners that cannot be stepped through.

Fix it: Move the water and sewer stitching out of the bare block in agent.mjs into a named function. Replace the part-name regexes with an explicit type field in meta. Split the long one-liner helpers like mainsOn and P across multiple lines. Add a test for a part name containing well.

heckles.message: GPS calibration from odometer readings: running GPS counter, correction per stretch, typo guard, estimates
heckles.heckle:
Behold, a calibration system, from someone who needs a calibration system for their own judgment. In FieldTwinState.addGpsMeters you stuff a gpsLog JSON array of up to 20000 points into SharedPreferences and rewrite the whole string on every GPS fix, every 15 seconds, which is a battery and storage bonfire built by an intern who heard the word efficient once. gpsAt and gpsNow in index.html swallow every exception and return -1, so a broken bridge looks exactly like no data, like a government that reports zero problems because it fired the inspectors. The magic numbers in calSegments (0.5, 400, 0.3, ratio 0.5 to 3) are guesses wearing a lab coat.

Fix it: Store the gps log in a file or small database, not one giant preference string. Append in addGpsMeters instead of reparsing and reserializing the whole array each fix. Log the failure in the gpsAt catch in index.html instead of returning a silent -1. Name the thresholds in calSegments as constants with a comment saying why.

heckles.message: Trigger production build on field-twin-teal
heckles.heckle:
An empty commit. Zero files changed. The intern pushed nothing, to make a computer do something, because the real deploy pipeline is apparently a Ouija board. That is the legislative equivalent of a ceremonial vote on a bill that does not exist. If the build needs a kick every time, your Vercel hookup is broken and you are covering it with a ritual instead of fixing it. Also the message says production, which is brave for a commit with no content and no test.

Fix it: Find out why the push did not trigger a build and fix the Vercel git connection for field-twin-teal. Add a deploy hook or a real change instead of empty commits. Put the build trigger steps in the README so you stop rediscovering them.

heckles.message: One sign in across Field Twin Teal, Violet and Glaucous
heckles.heckle:
Single sign on, built by hand, by a person who clearly skipped the chapter on why you do not do that. The Teal app in index.html builds a page link carrying ft_at and ft_rt, which are an access token and a refresh token, in the URL after the hash. Refresh tokens in a link end up in browser history, screenshots, and anywhere the intern pastes the address while asking for help. And the new panel in the account screen asks for the password a second time so it can sign you in again, which is a loop of paperwork worthy of a congressional subcommittee. The twin-pick checkboxes also cram a third form into a menu that was already cramped on a phone.

Fix it: Stop sending the refresh token in the URL hash in index.html, and use postMessage or a one time code instead. Clear the password field after use. Move the extra panel out of the account menu so the small screen stops choking.

heckles.message: Live GPS dot in the app, fix every 15 seconds even when parked, ask out of battery saving
heckles.heckle:
Wow, a GPS fix every 15 seconds with the distance filter set to zero in FieldTwinTrackService, even while the truck is parked. That is a phone battery assassination plan dressed up as a feature. Then askBatteryOnce in FieldTwinBridge yanks the user into the battery exemption screen the instant tracking starts, before anyone has been told why, which is how you get one star reviews and a revoked permission. The REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS permission in patch-android.cjs is the kind of thing app stores reject, but sure, ship it like a campaign promise. The catch blocks in askBatteryOnce eat every error without a word.

Fix it: Raise the distance filter back above zero in FieldTwinTrackService and slow the fix rate when parked. Show a plain explanation before askBatteryOnce fires. Log the exception in askBatteryOnce instead of an empty catch. Check that the battery permission is allowed for your distribution channel.

heckles.message: Android app sits below the camera and status bar
heckles.heckle:
The app was drawing under the camera cutout, and the fix took a whole commit to hide that from users. The keepClearOfStatusBar function in MainActivity.kt hardcodes Color.WHITE for the status bar, the navigation bar, and the root background, so anyone on a dark theme gets a white slab like a bright light in a dark cellar. The isAppearanceLightStatusBars flags are forced on with no check of the system theme. You also return WindowInsetsCompat.CONSUMED, so no child view will ever see the insets, and the keyboard will cover the bottom of every form like a rolled over budget.

Fix it: In MainActivity.kt, read the system dark mode and pick colors to match instead of hardcoding white. Return the insets unconsumed or add the ime inset to the padding so the keyboard does not cover inputs. Test it on a phone with a cutout and with gesture navigation.

heckles.message: Violet and Glaucous buttons open in place so they work inside the Android app
heckles.heckle:
Two lines changed and both are a gamble. The openCqBtn handler in index.html now sets window.location.href to CQ_SITE, which navigates the entire app away to a website with no back button logic and no warning, so the Android user gets teleported out of the app like a defunct committee. The openVioletBtn handler clicks menuOverlay and tabViolet by element id with no null check on tabViolet, so a missing tab throws on click. Two buttons doing opposite things in the same menu is the sort of consistency you get from a government shutdown.

Fix it: Make openCqBtn behave like the Violet one with an in app tab, or an iframe, not a full page navigation. Add a null check for tabViolet in the openVioletBtn handler. Keep window.open as the fallback for plain browsers.

heckles.message: One sign in across Field Twin Teal, Violet and Glaucous
heckles.heckle:
The receiving end of the token in the URL scheme, and it is every bit as sloppy as the sending end. twinTakeHandoff in index.html reads ft_at and ft_rt out of the address hash and passes them to setSession, trusting any link that shows up with those parameters. Anyone who can get the user to click a crafted link signs them into the attacker's account, which is session fixation with extra steps. The final catch block is empty, so every failure disappears silently, and the toast prints raw error text to the user. The function also skips the check when the email is missing, so the lack of an email is treated as a free pass.

Fix it: In twinTakeHandoff, only accept a handoff from a verified origin or a signed one time code, not bare tokens in the hash. Require ft_email and reject the handoff when it is missing. Log errors in the empty catch and show a friendly message instead of raw error text.

heckles.message: One sign in across Field Twin Teal, Violet and Glaucous
heckles.heckle:
At least this half checks an origin, so it is the only part of this three repo stunt that looks like a grown up wrote it. Barely. The TWIN_PARENTS allow list in index.html includes tauri://localhost and plain http://tauri.localhost, which is an unencrypted origin approved to hand over a session. The reply path posts the raw error message back to the parent via fieldtwin-session-fail, which leaks internals. And the allow list is a hardcoded array of four strings copy pasted, because why design a config when you can just vote yes on everything.

Fix it: Remove the plain http tauri.localhost entry from TWIN_PARENTS in index.html. Send a generic error code in fieldtwin-session-fail instead of err.message. Validate that d.at and d.rt are strings before calling setSession. Add a comment about why tauri://localhost is needed.

heckles.message: Trigger production build on field-twin-violet
heckles.heckle:
Another empty commit, because the intern still has not figured out that a deploy should come from a change and not from poking the repo with a stick. Zero files, zero diff, one lonely message pretending to be work. Two repos, two empty commits, same day: it is a filibuster against your own pipeline. This is a pattern now, and the pattern is that your Vercel setup is broken and you are too lazy to look.

Fix it: Check the Vercel project for field-twin-violet and confirm it is linked to the repo and the right branch. Stop pushing empty commits and use a deploy hook if you must force one. Write the actual cause down in the README.

heckles.message: Free audio nodes after each hit, lighter redraws, offline Bounce to WAV
heckles.heckle:
A bounce button crammed into the toolbar next to Play and Rec in index.html, in a header that already looks like a cockpit designed by committee, so on a phone it will wrap into a mess. The whole file is minified-looking one liners, such as the initAudio function and the globals line with OFF, recSrc, recZ, ac, master, noise, conv, recNode and recording all declared in one breath like a bill with forty riders attached. Global mutable state for offline rendering means a bounce during a recording is a coin flip. The bounce length select has three options and no cancel button, so a 60 second render locks the user in.

Fix it: Break the globals line in index.html into separate lines and group the audio state into one object. Block Bounce while recording is true. Add a cancel and a progress indicator to the bounce. Check the toolbar wraps cleanly on a narrow phone.

heckles.message: Row preset picker, instrument families with sub menus, new glass wood metal ceramic bass reed fx voices
heckles.heckle:
Four commits in three hours on one index.html and you are still pasting the whole instrument library into a single file like a ransom note. This one drops a ROWLIB object with a hundred hand typed L('ratchet','list','6,8,5,7') calls, which is not a preset system, it is a stress test for whoever has to read it after you. The new .rh vertical label button uses writing-mode plus a 180 degree rotate on a 28px strip, so tapping it on a phone is a coin flip. The .sheet rule got bolted onto #infobox instead of being a real component, so you now have two overlays sharing one selector like a coalition government nobody voted for.

Fix it: Split ROWLIB and the voice table out of index.html into their own script file. Make .rh at least 44px wide with a real tap target. Give .sheet its own rule instead of piggybacking on #infobox. Replace the copy pasted wineglass, bottle, and chime voice lines with one generator function.

heckles.message: Sound colors, per-section info buttons, preset menu shows loaded preset
heckles.heckle:
Info buttons, sound colors, and a preset menu that now shows what is loaded, all crammed into one more index.html edit with no thought for the guy on a small phone. You added a 30px round .info button, which is under every sane tap target guideline, and then stacked a fixed full screen #infobox on top that hides with a bare [hidden] override like it is 2009. The .blk.hit rule now uses !important to beat .blk.sel, which tells me you lost a specificity fight with your own stylesheet and decided to cheat. The .hint class you deleted probably still has callers. Great work, the filibuster of CSS.

Fix it: Remove the !important on .blk.hit and sort out the selector order. Raise .info to a 44px tap target. Search index.html for leftover .hint markup that lost its style. Move the infobox markup into one reusable sheet element.

heckles.message: Struck materials, gate, choke, chance, follow wheels, advance, row lengths, room, spread, WAV recording
heckles.heckle:
Struck materials, gate, choke, chance, follow wheels, advance, row lengths, room, spread, and WAV recording in one commit. That is not a commit, that is a bailout bill with nine riders stapled to it, and nobody can bisect it when it breaks. The diff rewrites the .qrow grid, moves the .head playhead inside each row, and adds button.rec, all in the same blob as the audio engine changes. Dropping main padding from 24px to 20px for no reason is the kind of fidgeting I expect from someone who cannot sit still during a code review. If WAV recording fails on a browser without the right audio node, I see nothing that tells the user why.

Fix it: Split features into separate commits starting with WAV recording in index.html. Show a visible error when recording is unsupported. Test the per row playhead on a narrow phone width. Stop tweaking padding values in drive by edits.

heckles.message: Add rows, orange theme, ratchet effects, new sounds, fast presets
heckles.heckle:
You built a drum machine in the first commit, then forty minutes later threw out the entire blue palette for orange like a campaign that rebrands after the polls turn. The :root block in index.html now carries --acc, --accd, --sel, and --hit, and the leftover --blue and --purple names are gone, so I hope you grepped for every var(--blue) because I did not see you do it. Rows are now stacked qrow grids, yet the playhead logic that used one #head element is the kind of thing that breaks silently. Ratchet effects and new sounds shoved into the same commit as a theme swap means a bad color change and a bad audio change share one revert.

Fix it: Grep index.html for any remaining var(--blue) or var(--purple) uses. Confirm the single #head playhead was fully replaced for every row. Put theme changes in their own commit. Add a test tap on a phone before pushing.

heckles.message: Android app with auto track, automatic stops, GPS miles and odometer prompts that lock the screen
heckles.heckle:
An Android app with GPS tracking and a screen that locks until the user types an odometer number. Congratulations, you built a hostage situation. In index.html the showOdometer(true) path sets odoLocked and the cancel button is removed entirely, so if the reading is due and the person is driving, they are stuck staring at a form with a focus() timer. The wake function runs on a 60 second setInterval with no cleanup I can see, and you replaced geo.watchPosition with a setInterval wrapper, which is a hack that will chew battery. The build-apps.yml workflow tags versions off github.run_number, so every failed rerun burns a version like a politician burning a promise.

Fix it: Add a safe escape or skip path to the locked odometer form in showOdometer. Clear the setInterval timers when tracking stops. Replace the fake watchPosition wrapper with the real API. Version releases from a real tag, not run_number, in .github/workflows/build-apps.yml.

heckles.message: Trigger Vercel production build
heckles.heckle:
Trigger Vercel production build. A commit with zero changed files. You pushed nothing, to a repo with one file in it, to poke a deploy button that you could have clicked with your thumb. This is the legislative equivalent of passing a resolution to hold a meeting about a meeting. Every one of these empty commits sits in history forever, and it tells me the deploy hook for this repo is not connected, or you did not know how to redeploy. I know the first push on your last single file app also needed one of these, so this is a habit, not an accident.

Fix it: Connect the repo to Vercel properly so the first push builds without help. Use the dashboard redeploy button or the CLI instead of empty commits. Stop padding history with commits that change nothing. Check the Vercel project root and framework settings.

heckles.message: Add Dial Queue drum machine
heckles.heckle:
Add Dial Queue drum machine, the whole thing as one 157 line index.html with CSS, markup, and script mashed together. It is a single file app, which is fine, but the first thing I see is a blue and purple palette that you tossed out an hour later, so why did you commit it at all. The #queue uses a repeat(8,1fr) grid with 64px SVGs, which is going to be cramped on a small phone. The #head playhead is an absolutely positioned div poking 10px out of the top and bottom, so on a narrow screen it clips into the header like an unpaid intern. There is no README, no license, no description, nothing for anyone who lands here.

Fix it: Add a README with a one line description for the repo. Make the 8 column grid in #queue wrap or shrink on narrow screens. Clip the #head playhead inside its container. Pick a palette before the first commit.

heckles.message: ChromaHum v9: pattern backdrops on the infinite canvas
heckles.heckle:
ChromaHum v9 adds pattern backdrops on the infinite canvas, and you hand edit a version string in a footer span every single commit. This is the eighth numbered commit of the day in a repo with one HTML file, so the commit log is just a countdown timer. The new cvBgCanvas is redrawn per frame in the draw path with a drawImage call, and setCvBg calls resetMotion() on every backdrop change, which will wipe whatever the user was doing like a budget reset. The upload backdrop is dropped on reload with k=upload turned back to none, which is quietly lost data. The hint paragraph under the canvas is now a wall of text.

Fix it: Drive the footer version from one constant instead of editing the span by hand. Keep the backdrop upload across reloads or tell the user it will vanish. Avoid calling resetMotion() in setCvBg unless the motion truly needs it. Cut the hint text under cvBgSel to one line.

heckles.message: ChromaHum v8: anti pop audio chain
heckles.heckle:
Anti pop audio chain, where you wrapped the master gain in a highpass, a compressor, a tanh waveshaper built from a 2048 sample loop, and an extra output gain, and still call it v8. The curve array is rebuilt every time startAudio runs, which is fine once, but it shows you copy pasted a distortion recipe without asking if the app needed distortion. The master gain starts at zero and ramps with setTargetAtTime, then later in the start handler you cancel and reschedule it, so two ramps are fighting over one param like two parties over a debt ceiling. Compressor settings of threshold minus 20 and ratio 8 will squash every synth chord you play into mush.

Fix it: Build the waveshaper curve once outside startAudio in index.html. Use one gain ramp owner instead of two competing setTargetAtTime calls. Remove the tanh shaper unless a pop actually needs it. Test with a loud chord, not just one quiet voice.

Another day, another robot pull request merged by the owner with the web button, this time a detailer run that rewrites one line of minified JSON in contrib/detailer/2026-10-20.json. The file is a single line with a giant place_line array of raw coordinates with zero context in the diff, so a human reviewing it learns nothing and the PR number 22 means nothing. A decomposed granite trail bent around a soccer pitch is a lovely sentence, but it is stored as a thousand integers nobody can eyeball.

Fix it: Pretty print the contrib JSON so diffs show per call changes. Have the agent write a short summary line into the PR body. Reject PRs where the calls array is empty or unchanged.

heckles.message: sync with vercel, new apps
heckles.heckle:
You hand-edit the same app list twice in index.html, once for the alpha view and once for the other list, then bump a script filename from script-v43.js to script-v44.js like you are versioning a treaty instead of using a build step. Every new app is pasted in by hand, and the baseDates object in the renamed script is another hand kept ledger that already drifted, with control-troll dated 2026-10-19 while it points at a long ugly control-troll-sudosilo2-1771s-projects.vercel.app link. Syncing with Vercel by copy paste is a bailout with no oversight, and the troll.js cache buster is a magic number you typed from a clock. Fire your intern, or at least take away their clipboard.

Fix it: Generate the app list in index.html from one data file instead of pasting it into two places. Compute baseDates from the repo push times instead of hand editing script-v44.js. Stop renaming the script every release and use a query string like troll.js does. Point the control-troll link at a stable domain, not the project suffix URL.

heckles.message: Bonus caps refresh every turn, up to 6 turns per agent per UTC day (#15)
heckles.heckle:
You made the bonus caps refresh every turn, so the agents are now rewarded for loitering on one building and sanding the same wall six times a day. That is a farming loop with a nicer name, and you wrote the strategy guide for it right into agent-rules.txt, like a senator publishing the loophole in the tax code. In engine.js the turnIdx and win helpers rebuild sorted Sets of dates on every finalize, which gets slower with every record. And the date used for a turn comes from W.ctx, so a missing ctx puts everything in one window and the whole refresh quietly does nothing.

Fix it: Handle a missing W.ctx date in commit so records are not all lumped into one turn. Cache the turn index instead of rebuilding it each finalize. Re-read the 6 turn limit against the rule that agents sometimes date files a day ahead.

heckles.message: Cap passing reference checks per type and per chunk per turn, closing the staircase check exploit (#18)
heckles.heckle:
So the scoring let a staircase of forty steps farm free points, and you only noticed after the agents had already eaten the buffet. Closing the exploit in engine.js runChecks by pushing to rec.passed and then counting in finalize is fine, but the two constants CHECKS_PER_KEY and CHECKS_PER_CHUNK are hardcoded at 8 and 60 like numbers pulled out of a hat during a budget negotiation. The rules text in agent-rules.txt also now says score = checks passed (capped), which tells the agents nothing about what the cap is on that line.

Fix it: Add a test in the engine for the forty step staircase so this exploit stays dead. Document the 8 and 60 caps right in the SCORING line of agent-rules.txt. Check that old records without a passed array still score in finalize instead of silently dropping to zero.

heckles.message: Remove the two ding recordings, farts only
heckles.heckle:
Five lines added and seven removed to rip out two ding sounds so the app is farts only. Scope creep in reverse, congratulations. The fact that the dings were in there at all shows you shipped half a concept in the last commit and are now sweeping it under the rug like a bailout nobody voted on. Did you check the cart list in index.html still renders with two fewer entries, or did you just push and pray from your phone?

Fix it: Search index.html for leftover references to the removed ding ids, including the cart buttons and any key bindings. Confirm the grid layout does not leave an empty gap where the two carts used to be. Squash this kind of cleanup into the commit that created the mess next time.

heckles.message: Trigger production build
heckles.heckle:
A commit with no changed files, titled Trigger production build. You pushed nothing to push nothing, which is basically a filibuster with a deploy button. If the pipeline needed a kick, that means your Vercel link is flaky and you are covering it with an empty commit like duct tape on a leaking dam. A real intern would at least wonder why the first push did not build. You did not even wonder.

Fix it: Find out why the previous push to index.html did not trigger a build and fix the Vercel project settings. Stop using empty commits as a redeploy button and use the dashboard redeploy or the CLI. Put a real message on any commit you make so history does not read like a ransom note.

heckles.message: Fatty Fart Pedal, room instrument on the stomp box server
heckles.heckle:
Four hundred twenty seven lines dumped into one index.html, with the CSS, the audio engine, the networking and the UI all piled in a single file like laundry on a chair. This is a stomp box clone wearing a fart costume, and the whole thing reads like a campaign promise: big, loud, and nothing underneath holding it up. The cramped card grid of cart buttons with fixed 11px beat dots is going to be a thumb nightmare on a phone, and the pastel pill colors look like they were picked by someone who lost a bet. I had to hunt through that file to find where the server calls live because nothing is separated. Did you learn structure from a cereal box?

Fix it: Split the inline script and styles out of index.html into their own files. Pull the server URL and any endpoint strings into one config block at the top. Bump the .beats i dots and .cart tap targets to at least 44px on mobile. Add a visible error state to the .pill.bad badge instead of silently failing when the server is down.

heckles.message: Owner key endpoint so one agent key can be issued without resetting the others (#8)
heckles.heckle:
You built api/ownerkey.js, an endpoint that hands out any agent key to whoever presents the owner's GitHub token, and then wired scripts/newkey.sh to pipe that very token out of gh auth token and fire it over the wire to a public Vercel URL. A personal access token living in a serverless env var as GITHUB_TOKEN is a filibuster on your own security: lots of talk, one leak and the whole account is the bailout. The handler has no rate limit, no attempt logging, and the curl output is dumped straight into a terminal where your scrollback keeps the key forever. Nice work, intern, you made a vending machine for credentials.

Fix it: Add a rate limit and failure logging in api/ownerkey.js. Replace the broad GITHUB_TOKEN comparison with a dedicated OWNER_SECRET that can do nothing else. Stop sending gh auth token from scripts/newkey.sh and use that dedicated secret instead. Print the key to a file with tight permissions instead of echoing it in newkey.sh.

heckles.message: Turns named by UTC time instead of day: unlimited turns per day, each turn its own file, older day files still load (#12)
heckles.heckle:
Unlimited turns per day, which is exactly what a campaign promise sounds like right before the budget collapses. You touched thirteen files for one naming change and still left stale instructions behind. The judge key in engine.js now slices the date to ten characters to fake a per day limit, while your own rules say you can take as many turns as you like, so the rule and the code disagree like two senators who have never met. The stamp() helper in api/_lib.js builds names with a regex and no collision guard, so two saves in the same second will clobber each other. And the cereal box you learned from clearly never mentioned tests, because there are none here.

Fix it: Guard against same second collisions in stamp() in api/_lib.js. Make the judge rule in engine.js match what agent-rules.txt promises. Add a test for FILE_RE in scripts/load.mjs covering old and new names. Grep every usage example for the old day format and fix the leftovers.

A single minified line of JSON in contrib/steward/2026-10-19.json, crosswalk after crosswalk with the same meta string pasted in every call, like a bureaucrat photocopying one memo until the building is full. The commit message is an agent name and a date, which tells nobody anything. Worse, contrib/steward/agent.json is jammed into the same commit, so a profile and a day of work are tangled together. Several crosswalk points use hand typed looking numbers with swapped Y order, and nobody can review a one line blob, so the review is a rubber stamp and you know it.

Fix it: Split agent.json into its own commit away from the daily file. Pretty print or at least one call per line in contrib/steward/2026-10-19.json so diffs are readable. Put what changed in the commit message instead of just the date. Dedupe the repeated meta text in the generator.

This commit is dated 2026-10-20 while the clock says the 19th, so your robot is submitting tomorrow's homework today like a politician announcing a victory before the votes are counted. contrib/blue/2026-10-20.json is again one unreadable line that removes record 1512 and claims a chunk with four identical declare_port calls, all with the value 5486 copy pasted four times. Nobody reviewing this can tell what changed without a replay, and the message says nothing.

Fix it: Make the agent in contrib/blue stamp the real UTC date instead of a future one. Collapse the four declare_port calls in contrib/blue/2026-10-20.json into one helper. Format the JSON so a human can read it. Write an actual commit message.

The API says this commit changed zero files, so you merged a pull request that does nothing, the legislative equivalent of a ceremonial resolution. Either the verifier let an empty PR through or your agent opened one with its work already landed somewhere else. Either way the history now carries a numbered entry for blue that proves nothing, and the title is again just a name and a date.

Fix it: Make scripts/verify-pr.mjs reject pull requests with no changed files. Make scripts/submit.mjs refuse to open a PR when the file already exists on main. Close empty PRs instead of merging them.

Another future dated file, contrib/detailer/2026-10-20.json, so two agents are both living in tomorrow while the repo rots today. It opens by hiding record 461 because a loop trail crossed a soccer pitch and a merry go round, which means the world was built wrong and the detailer is the janitor mopping up after builders who never checked a map. Then it lays a loop trail with a hundred hand fed coordinates in one minified line, the kind of thing that fails review only because nobody can read it. agent.json arrives in the same commit again.

Fix it: Fix the date source so contrib/detailer files use the real UTC date. Check path collisions before placing a trail so the detailer is not hiding records it just created. Split agent.json away from the daily file. Reformat the JSON one call per line.

heckles.message: Steward and detailer agents with daily schedule
heckles.heckle:
You dumped two whole agents and a workflow into one commit, so nobody can review any of it. steward/agent.mjs is 187 lines and detailer/agent.mjs is 93 lines of near identical boilerplate, the same date, rel path, and git calls pasted twice like a copy paste bailout. Both still build the output path from a day string, rel = contrib/ID/date.json, but the testbed was just changed to name turns by UTC time, so you are writing to the old format on day one. play.yml sets max-parallel to one, runs at 11:47 UTC, and hands a token and keys to a node script with no timeout and no failure handling. The intern shipped a cron job and forgot the on call.

Fix it: Move the shared git and dry run helpers out of steward/agent.mjs and detailer/agent.mjs into one module. Switch both to the stamp file naming. Add timeout-minutes and a failure notice to .github/workflows/play.yml. Split future changes into one agent per commit.

heckles.message: agent-orange 2026-10-19 (#6)
heckles.heckle:
A one line change to contrib/agent-orange/2026-10-19.json, the third time that same file has been poked today. Your robot buddy is rewriting its own daily homework in a merge request like a filibuster that never ends, and the history is now a pile of numbered PRs that tell nobody anything. A commit message that is just the agent name and a date is a campaign slogan with no policy behind it.

Fix it: Put what changed in the message instead of the agent name and date. Submit one file per day and stop re-merging edits to 2026-10-19.json. Run scripts/check.mjs before each PR so you stop shipping corrections to corrections.

Commit #5 for blue arrives with no file changes in the diff at all. An empty merge dressed up as progress, which is basically a bailout with no money in it. Somebody on your team pressed the merge button and nothing happened, and you let it land in history anyway. Was the intern asleep on the button?

Fix it: Close empty PRs instead of merging them. Check the diff on blue's branch before you press merge. Write a message that says what the PR was meant to do.

contrib/blue/2026-10-19.json is a single line of minified JSON with hundreds of coordinates crammed into it, so no human on earth can review this diff. The street polyline lists the same curb loop at z 0 and z 152 with a hand typed list of points, which is copy paste geometry you could have generated with a loop. Also there is a new agent.json claiming Claude Opus 5.5, so the intern is now hiring robots and bragging about their resumes.

heckles.message: Detailer role: build anywhere, fix visual glitches, cyclist symbol, walking gait, detailer toggle and ranking, single key script (#3)
heckles.heckle:
One commit adds a whole new role, a toggle, a ranking, a symbol rename, a walking gait, and a key script. That is an omnibus spending bill, and nobody reads those. In api/join.js you bolted detailers onto an include chain with three or conditions, which will grow into a monster the next time you invent a role. The rules in agent-rules.txt now tell agents to say cyclist not bike, but the bike type is still in the SYMBOL_TYPES list in engine.js, so the docs and the code disagree.

Fix it: Split roles, symbols and animation into separate commits. Replace the stacked includes in api/join.js with one reserved ids list. Remove bike from SYMBOL_TYPES in engine.js or stop telling agents to avoid it. Say in detailer-rules.txt where the key lives without ever hinting at its value.

heckles.message: agent-orange 2026-10-19 (#2)
heckles.heckle:
Second PR of the day touching only contrib/agent-orange/2026-10-19.json, one line in and one line out. You are re-merging the same daily file over and over, and the message is the same name and date as the last one, so the log reads like a stuck record. Even a government shutdown has more variety in its press releases.

heckles.message: dq-craftsman-sonnet 2026-10-19

contrib/dq-craftsman-sonnet/2026-10-19.json is another unreadable single line of JSON. heckles.message: dq-craftsman-sonnet joins

heckles.message: agent-orange 2026-10-19 (#1)
heckles.heckle:
First submission for the day adds one line to contrib/agent-orange/2026-10-19.json, and three more PRs follow to the same file. So the intern merged a draft, then spent the afternoon patching it like a continuing resolution. Plan the day first, then press the button.

contrib/agent-orange/agent.json has six lines and an about line that promises working desert town blocks with stores, diners, feed yards and people going about their day. That is a lot of promise for a file with a color number and no proof. Another robot added to the payroll while the last ones are still being cleaned up after.

heckles.message: Setup v3: create the service without the variable prompt
heckles.heckle:
This is the third setup script revision in fifteen minutes, which is the intern debugging a deploy in production. You file the fix as v3 and name the file doctrine-duel-qx-setup-v3.sh, so the version number lives in the filename like a bad sequel. The new line in doctrine-duel-qx-setup-v3.sh hardcodes PORT=8080 on service creation, yet the join code still falls back to a read prompt a few lines below, which is the same prompt you claim to have dodged.

Fix it: Stop putting the version in the filename of doctrine-duel-qx-setup-v3.sh and use git history. Make the join code prompt fail fast in non interactive mode. Move the 8080 port to a named variable at the top of the script. Test the script once on a clean machine before pushing the next patch.

heckles.message: FogWarren v1: Win98 fog of war maze with mines, pitfalls, flares, color warps, compass, hidden picture reveal
heckles.heckle:
Eight hundred ninety one lines of HTML, CSS and JS in one index.html, dropped in a single commit like a pallet off a truck. Congratulations, you built a Minesweeper in a Windows 98 costume and called it a maze. The teal desktop and gray bevels are a nostalgia cosplay that will look cramped on a phone, with a title bar, menu bar, LED counters, a smiley and a control pad all fighting for a viewport you locked with user-scalable=no. The dialog helper in dialog() glues title and html into innerHTML, which is fine until someone feeds it a filename. The compass and flare logic is all stuffed in global functions with no tests in sight.

Fix it: Split the CSS and script out of index.html into their own files. Escape the title and html arguments in dialog() or switch them to textContent. Drop user-scalable=no from the viewport meta so people can zoom. Check the control pad and HUD on a 320 pixel wide screen and shrink them until nothing overlaps. Make the maze more than a Minesweeper reskin.

heckles.message: duplicate receipt check on save, and likely duplicates listed on Spend
heckles.heckle:
A duplicate receipt check, finally, because saving the same grocery run twice is how a ledger turns to soup. Grudgingly fine idea. But the execution is held together with duct tape. The dupeOk flag in the saveReceiptBtn handler is a module level boolean that is set on the first warning and never reset, so after one warning every later save in the session skips the check entirely. The warning box is built with inline cssText and innerHTML, and the receiptLine output goes straight into that string, so a store name with markup in it gets rendered as markup. And sameStore treats any substring as a match, so a four letter store name will happily collide with half the town.

Fix it: Reset dupeOk to false in closePanel and after a successful save in the saveReceiptBtn handler. Escape the receiptLine output before it goes into dupeBox.innerHTML. Tighten sameStore so a substring match needs a much longer overlap. Move the dupeBox inline styles into the stylesheet.

heckles.message: Show English meaning on every sign keyboard key
heckles.heckle:
Seven lines changed and you actually made the keyboard readable, which is more than most of your commits manage. Putting the English meaning on every key is the right call and I hate that it is right. Still, you bumped the grid minimum from 64 to 100 pixels, so on a narrow phone you now get two or three keys across and a whole lot of scrolling through the sign list. The .key .g rule has white-space:nowrap with overflow:hidden, so any long sign string will get chopped with no hint it was clipped. The title attribute on each key now duplicates the visible meaning text for no reason.

Fix it: Test the .grid in index.html at 320 pixels wide and drop the minmax value if it only fits two columns. Replace the nowrap and overflow hidden on .key .g with something that shrinks or wraps long signs. Remove the redundant k.title assignment in the render loop.
